title: Put care management on a defensible footing
objective: Bill care management only where consent, a care plan and logged time support the code, and settle what to do about past claims.
impact_note: Protects a revenue line of about $165,000 a year at October's volume and today's paid rate (about $370,000 if every line were paid) and limits repayment exposure.
success_measures: No care-management claim is sent for November 2026 or any later month unless it traces to a consent, a care plan and a time log
Total minutes billed in a month do not exceed the hours the staff and the physician had available
The attorney has given written advice on past claims
steps: Decide which code each patient's records support
Build the time log and consent fields
Review of past claims as the attorney directs

title: Independent audit of visit levels and documentation
objective: Learn whether the notes support the levels billed, for both clinicians, before anyone else asks.
impact_note: Protects about $600,000 a year of visit revenue. An audit of 80 to 100 notes typically costs a few thousand dollars.
success_measures: A written audit report covering every main code family for both clinicians
A decision, on advice, about any overpayment
A quarterly audit on the calendar
steps: Attorney engages the auditor and sets in advance the error rate that will trigger a larger sample
Auditor draws a documented random sample of 10 notes per code family per clinician
If errors are found: handle those claims on the attorney's advice and size the rest from every affected claim or a statistically valid random sample
Attorney decides what is shared with the clinicians for education
Quarterly follow-up audits as routine compliance work

title: Capture payer status and place of service at the source
objective: Know for every resident and every date whether they are in a Medicare Part A skilled stay, on hospice or in a Medicare Advantage plan, and bill accordingly.
impact_note: One time, for 2026 visits. Correct setting codes, recovery of 2026 visits underpaid at the skilled-stay rate, and fewer wrong-payer denials. Higher care-management payments are not counted until the care-management review is done.
success_measures: Each facility sends a weekly census with skilled-stay status and payer
Place of service 31 or 32 is set from that census on every nursing facility claim

For each hospice patient the system flags the hospice election, and the clinician records two facts for the visit: whether he or she is the attending clinician the patient named, and whether the visit relates to the terminal illness. The claim then carries the matching modifier (GV for a related visit by the named attending clinician, GW for an unrelated visit), or the visit is billed to the hospice
steps: Ask each facility for the census
Store status with the patient by date
Set place of service from it
Measure three months of past claims

title: Finish the coverage refresh and verify monthly
objective: No charge without a verified payer, and every active patient re-verified on the first of each month.
impact_note: 11.2% of charges had no payer when entered. Coverage and wrong-payer problems are about a quarter of denied visits.
success_measures: All 493 coverage cards verified or marked self-pay
Charges with no payer under 2%
A re-verification run on the first of each month
steps: Hold claims with no verified payer

title: Collect the aged receivables before filing windows close
objective: Work the correct-and-resend list ($65,431 when it was tagged on October 16, 2026; refresh it first) and the 74 actionable denials, oldest deadline first.
impact_note: One-time cash, estimated at about 40% of billed charges on the items worked.
success_measures: Correct-and-resend list at zero
Dollars collected on balances older than 90 days, reported each week beside dollars written off
No claim lost to a filing deadline in December
steps: Appeal where resending will not work

title: Close the enrollment and credentialing gaps
objective: Both clinicians enrolled and current with every payer the patients have, starting with Medicaid.
impact_note: Keeps Medicaid and Medicaid plan payments and stops avoidable denials. 108 denied visits are tagged credentialing.
success_measures: Medicaid renewal filed before December 1 and confirmed
No open item on the credentialing board older than 60 days
One expiry calendar with 90-day warnings
steps: Nurse practitioner revalidation and national record

title: Match every deposit to a remittance
objective: Know that every dollar paid reached the bank and every deposit was posted.
impact_note: One time. The $12,902 of unmatched Medicare deposits is cash already received. Remittances with no deposit have not been totaled, so the range is a placeholder.
success_measures: A weekly match with nothing unexplained older than 10 days
Electronic remittance and deposit active for every payer that offers it

title: Monthly close and monthly owner review
objective: Run the practice from one page of numbers once a month.
impact_note: No direct dollar value. It is how every other project stays done.
success_measures: Books closed by the 15th of each month
A 45-minute review held and decisions logged, three months running
A 2027 budget with four scenarios

title: A compliance program sized for two clinicians
objective: A short written program that the practice actually follows.
impact_note: Changes how any future billing problem is treated.
success_measures: A written program adopted and dated
Training done and recorded for both clinicians
Medical director agreements and time logs reviewed by the attorney
A security risk analysis on file

title: Tighten controls on automation and access
objective: Keep the speed of agent-run billing while proving it is doing the right thing.
impact_note: Reduces the chance that one wrong rule repeats across hundreds of claims.
success_measures: Open sign-up turned off
The shared access key replaced
A monthly sample of 25 automated actions reviewed and logged
steps: Switch off three standing billing rules

title: Find out where the practice stands in Medicare's quality program
objective: Avoid a penalty of up to 9% of Medicare payments.
impact_note: Penalty avoided, if either clinician is required to report.
success_measures: Status known for both clinicians
A reporting plan for the 2026 performance year, decided by early December 2026

title: Deliver and bill the services patients already qualify for
objective: Add wellness visits, transitional care and properly documented advance care planning.
impact_note: About 150 wellness visits a year and a few transitional care services a month.
success_measures: Wellness visits scheduled for long-term residents
Transitional care billed for patients discharged to assisted living or home
A time statement in every advance care planning note (the work item sits with the coding audit, due December 4, 2026)

title: Know the contracts and the 2027 rates
objective: Hold every payer contract and fee schedule and check payments against them.
impact_note: Underpayments found, denials disputed with the contract in hand, and no surprise from the 2027 Medicare changes.
success_measures: A contract and fee schedule on file for every plan
The top 15 codes repriced for 2027 by site of service
Payments below the expected amount flagged automatically

title: Debt, the owner's loan and tax
objective: Lower the cost of debt, clear the amount owed by the owner, and set pay on a defensible basis.
impact_note: Interest saved by refinancing. The larger value is a clean balance sheet before any sale.
success_measures: A refinancing decision on the 13.99% note
A written plan for the shareholder loan
Salary level reviewed
A cash floor of 90 days agreed

title: Reduce dependence on the owner and on a few sites
objective: Make the revenue and the know-how survive the owner's absence.
impact_note: Protects revenue and is the main lever on sale value.
success_measures: A written emergency plan and a covering physician
A second clinician introduced at every site
A record of contacts and agreements for each site

title: Add a second nurse practitioner when the numbers support it
objective: Grow revenue and spread the census across more clinicians.
impact_note: Contribution after cost once the new clinician is fully busy: about $30,000 at 13.4 visits a day and about $90,000 at 17. A loss below about 12 a day.
success_measures: A written case with census, ramp and enrollment timing
A decision made

title: Build the file a buyer would ask for
objective: Be able to answer a buyer's first twenty requests from one folder, whether or not the practice is ever sold.
impact_note: Supports the multiple. Each $100,000 of proven earnings is worth about $300,000 of price.
success_measures: Twelve months of monthly statements
Contracts, routine audit summaries cleared by the attorney and credentialing in one folder
A refreshed valuation
